title: Moonshot AI Opens Kimi Research Support Program: For Natural Sciences and Engineering Disciplines, Providing API Credits and Technical Support
excerpt: Some topics in the research world are clearly important, yet go untouched year after year—they have small audiences, long timelines, slow returns, span multiple
content_html:
Some topics in the research world are clearly important, yet go untouched year after year—they have small audiences, long timelines, slow returns, span multiple disciplines, and do not fit neatly into the pigeonholes of existing research systems. Moonshot AI has decided to offer a ladder to these “cold-bench” research areas: on the morning of November 27, Moonshot AI announced that the Kimi Research Support Program is officially open for applications. The first phase is aimed at researchers in the natural sciences, engineering, and related interdisciplinary fields, and selected applicants will receive Kimi API credits and technical support from the team.

Resources Follow the Research

According to the official announcement, support is offered at three tiers: API credits are determined based on research needs and review results; selected applicants can also get priority access to new models and obtain curated research and community resources; outstanding researchers and teams will receive longer-term and more in-depth technical and resource support. The application portal is now live on the Kimi official website. Interested researchers can simply submit their materials and wait for review.

AI Fills the Corners That Funding Cannot Reach

Moonshot AI spelled out this logic plainly in the announcement: from life and health to energy and materials, from the frontiers of basic science to unknown fields, countless important scientific questions remain to be answered. Some of them serve only relatively small groups of people, some have long research cycles and limited short-term returns, and some span multiple disciplines and are difficult for existing systems to fully cover—“They have not been fully explored, but that does not mean they are not important.” The company believes that AI can lower the barrier to exploring these questions, so that research with long-term value is not held back by resource constraints, and so that truly talented researchers can push forward the questions they care about. As the company puts it, this broad, sustained, and open capacity for exploration is the shared foundation for humanity’s continued scientific progress.
